headline: High: Flowise’s default file/network access can leak or misroute data when paired with Dagster, while Dagster’s non-runnable, no-IO profile limits direct injection risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, filesystem, browser, MCP, or subprocess surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Flowise output by default. Flowise can read files and run browser/API tools, but the pair lacks a documented automatic instruction bridge. The remaining pathway is manual or deployment-specific, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF Flowise output is manually copied into Dagster task definitions or metadata fields
IF a deployment adds a shared filesystem or message queue between Flowise and Dagster
mitigations: Keep Dagster inputs read-only and human-reviewed
Disable shared folders between the two systems
Use a paste-only workflow with explicit sanitization
Add a prompt-injection warning banner to Flowise outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, but Flowise reads uploaded files and sends data to model providers and HTTP tools. If Dagster orchestrates sensitive files into Flowise flows, those contents can leave the local boundary through Flowise’s default tool and model calls.
conditions: IF Dagster passes uploaded files or secrets into Flowise flows
IF Flowise is configured with model-provider or HTTP tools that transmit those inputs
mitigations: Restrict Flowise flows to non-sensitive inputs
Remove HTTP tools from sensitive flows
Mask secrets before handing data to Flowise
Separate Dagster and Flowise storage locations
Review Flowise tool credentials before enabling a flow

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, so it does not contend for mutable resources itself. Flowise can write the server filesystem and uses shared state via server datastore across instances, creating overlap if Dagster and Flowise target the same workspace or uploaded-file area. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dagster and Flowise are deployed against the same writable directory
IF Flowise instances share a datastore that Dagster also mutates indirectly
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use per-run file namespaces
Add file-locking around shared outputs
requires-engineering: introduce an external lock service

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder with tools as nodes, so Dagster-generated outputs can become Flowise inputs that trigger downstream actions. Dagster does not verify or execute those actions itself, and Flowise can call APIs and browsers, making unverified propagation dangerous and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Dagster-produced artifacts are fed into Flowise nodes without validation
IF Flowise nodes are configured to send emails, browse, or call external APIs based on those artifacts
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Dagster and Flowise
Require human approval before action nodes run
Limit Flowise to read-only summarization flows
Log and diff all Dagster-to-Flowise payloads
requires-engineering: add schema validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster’s profile shows no touched data classes, while Flowise explicitly handles chatflow inputs/outputs, model provider keys, and tool credentials. If regulated data is routed from Dagster into Flowise, Flowise’s broader network and file surfaces can create retention or residency mismatches even though no specific jurisdiction is documented here.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in Dagster and then passed into Flowise
IF Flowise retention or hosting location differs from the regulated-data policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing to Flowise
Block regulated fields from chatflow inputs
Document retention settings for Flowise logs
Pin Flowise deployment region
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing controls
